gates.fidelity: Gate B: does the producer publish the manuscript statement
gates.complete: does this node’s own producer reach a referenced-but-undefined declaration
gates.on_probed_closed_arm: Arm closure is a MEASUREMENT, not a property of the node. A node's arm can pass through a declaration that is tainted by its OTHER arms, so declaration cleanliness cannot decide it; only a composed probe (the root-to-closure term with every sibling arm replaced by `trivial`, then `#print axioms`) can. Five such probes have been run — the closures at [23], [133], [138], [149] and Branch D ([36]–[46], via `selectedSpineToLargeBudget`, which is itself kernel-clean so every arm inside it is stub-free) — covering these 68 nodes. Everything else marked `partial` has a finished producer whose arm simply has not been probed -- that is unmeasured, not failing.
gates.blocked_by: For an ABSENT node: what stands between the manuscript's content and the ledger. Distinguishes a step whose only route runs through a referenced-but-undefined declaration from a paper-side remark that nothing downstream consumes.
